- [USER] User expressed interest in notable examples of Moorish architecture in Andalusia, Spain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Alhambra: Built in the 14th century, located in Granada, famous example of Moorish architecture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mezquita of Cordoba: Also known as the Great Mosque of Cordoba, originally built in the 8th century, features over 850 columns of jasper, onyx, and marble.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Alcazar of Seville: Originally built in the 10th century, a palace complex featuring a mix of Moorish, Gothic, and Renaissance architecture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Giralda Tower: Originally built as a minaret for the Great Mosque of Seville in the 12th century, notable example of Moorish architecture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nasrid Palaces: Located within the Alhambra in Granada, feature intricate carvings, arches, and columns typical of Moorish design.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Alcazaba of Malaga: A fortified palace complex built in the 11th century, features a mix of Islamic and Christian design elements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Medina Azahara: A ruined city near Cordoba built in the 10th century, features expansive courtyards and ornate decoration.
